sizing_basis: unsold 2,520 MT at replacement value x grade factor 0.696786; k = 79.0116 ₹/t per USD/t, one lot = 422.05 ₹ per USD/t
basis_risk_note: MCX Aluminium is a primary-ingot contract priced at duty-paid import parity; the desk is long Zorba 95/5 scrap whose CFR price is a reconstructed percentage of LME 3M. The hedge covers the LME leg of the exposure and nothing else: if the Zorba discount narrows or widens, that lands in the grade-spread bucket, not in the hedge, and on this ticket it is the larger number of the two. Three further mismatches are carried knowingly — LME official cash is fixed at the London midday ring while MCX settles in the Indian evening; the duty-parity relationship can break, as it visibly did in the first week of March 2022; and the physical cargo's duty base runs on the CBIC notified rate while MCX's uplift runs on the market rate. In base runs the panel MCX series is itself a parity proxy, so the measured cross-exchange basis is zero by construction and only the third-party mirror run shows it. The line is split 200/100 lots from the outset because the cargo is expected to be sold in two parcels, and a tranche is lifted as each sale fixes its price. The hedge goes on the day AFTER the trade: the near-month contract moved 12.0 % on the trade date, past the 9 % maximum daily price limit (mcx_al_dpl_max_frac), so it would have been limit-locked and no short could have been filled. The desk carries one session of the cargo unhedged and says so rather than claiming a fill it could not have had.

sizing_basis: S1 MCX-average leg 1,200 MT x 0.916; purchase leg floating x factor 0.638; k = 78.8355 ₹/t per USD/t, one lot = 421.00 ₹ per USD/t
basis_risk_note: Both legs float, but against different exchanges, different references and different months: the purchase settles on the LME official cash average for the month after shipment, the sale on the MCX near-month average over nine days in April. Until the sale prices, the desk is net long roughly a third of a tonne of LME-equivalent metal per tonne of scrap — the sale's recovery factor grossed up by duty parity (0.916 x 1.0825) less the purchase factor 0.638 — so the hedge starts short. Once the sale's average is behind us and the purchase's is not, the position is short the full purchase factor and the hedge flips long. What no hedge can cover here is the gap between MCX duty-paid primary parity and an LME-priced scrap cargo, nor the fact that the two averaging windows do not overlap at all; the desk treats an averaging leg as fully open before its window and closed after its midpoint trading day, which is an approximation and is the reason the flip is one decision rather than nine. In base runs the panel MCX series is a parity proxy, so the reported basis is zero by construction.

sizing_basis: unsold 1,260 MT at replacement value x grade factor 0.726000; k = 78.2376 ₹/t per USD/t, one lot = 416.90 ₹ per USD/t
basis_risk_note: Same cross-exchange mismatch as every other ticket in this book — MCX prices duty-paid primary ingot, the desk owns LME-linked Taint/Tabor scrap, so the hedge covers the metal leg and leaves the grade spread in its own bucket. What is different here is the size: 0.50 of the LME-equivalent delta rather than the desk's usual 0.90. The reason is written down on the trade date, not after it. First, the March variation-margin call on the short book was the largest cash outflow the desk had taken and the line has not been rebuilt; a smaller short is a smaller margin commitment through a market that has already shown it can move 12 % in a session. Second, on this grade the point-in-time screen says the scrap discount, not the flat price, is where the risk lives, and the MCX contract does not hedge the discount at any ratio. This is a deliberate decision to carry roughly 435 tonnes of LME-equivalent length unhedged, and if the market keeps falling it will cost money.

sizing_basis: S1 MCX-average leg 2,100 MT x 0.916; purchase leg floating x factor 0.702; k = 78.5977 ₹/t per USD/t, one lot = 418.27 ₹ per USD/t

When the purchase quotational period closes first the long becomes the whole cargo, so the hedge is increased by 279 lots rather than lifted, and both lines come off together when the sale's window passes its midpoint. The unhedgeable parts are the same as elsewhere: MCX prices duty-paid primary metal, the desk owns Tense scrap, and the two averaging windows do not overlap. In base runs the panel MCX series is a parity proxy, so the measured cross-exchange basis is zero by construction.
